units: Ps. XXXIV, 9),] to examine, to taste, test, try, experience.
<cite ref="Yoma 22b:17">Yoma 22ᵇ</cite> <he>לא ט׳ טַעַם חטא</he> never tasted the taste of sin (was innocent).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 5:2:2">Y. Succ. V, 55ᵇ</cite> <he>לא היו טוֹעֲמִין טעם וכ׳</he> had not even a taste of sleep.
<cite ref="Berakhot 35a:2">Ber. 35ᵃ</cite> <he>אסור … שיִטְעוֹם וכ׳</he> one must not taste food without a blessing.

<cite ref="Berakhot 14a:7">Ib. 14ᵃ</cite> <he>מהו שיטעום</he> dare he (who fasts) taste food when cooking? <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 7">Num. R. s. 7</cite> <he>כל מי … היה טוֹעֲמוֹ</he> whoever desired to eat meat felt its taste (in the mannah); a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Nedarim 66b:2">Ned. 66ᵇ</cite> <he>עד שתַּטְעִימִי … לרב וכ׳</he> until thou makest R. J. taste of thy dish.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 75a:10">B. Mets. 75ᵃ</cite> <he>כדי להַטְעִימָן וכ׳</he> in order to give them a taste of usury (that they might feel its oppressiveness).
Cant. R. to VII, 2 תהא … ומטעמני (read ומַטְעִימֵנִי or ומְטַעֲמֵנִי Pi.) thou shalt bring some of them before me and let me taste them; a. fr.
<cite ref="Sotah 21b:6">Sot. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>המַטְעִים דבריו וכ׳</he> who explains his case to the judge (trying to preoccupy him), before his adversary appears; Tanḥ.
